# AlterInForeach

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Performance](/rules/#performance) · PhpStorm name: `AlterInForeachInspection`

Three related `foreach` value-variable pitfalls:

1. a by-reference value (`as &$v`) that stays alive after the loop, so a later
   write to `$v` silently modifies the last array element;
2. an `unset($v)` right after a loop whose `$v` was *not* a reference (the
   unset is pointless, probably a leftover);
3. (opt-in) writing back through `$array[$key] = …` inside
   `foreach ($array as $key => $value)` where a by-reference value would do.

## Example

```php{4,6,8,13}
<?php
function adjust(array $prices, array $tags) {
    foreach ($prices as $sku => $amount) {
        $prices[$sku] = $amount * 2;
    }
    unset($sku, $amount);

    foreach ($tags as &$tag) {
        foreach ($prices as $p) {
            echo $tag, $p;
        }
    }
    unset($p);

    foreach ($tags as &$t) { $t = trim($t); }
    /** trimmed */
    unset($t);

    if ($tags) {
        foreach ($tags as & $u) { $u .= '!'; }
    }
    return $tags;
}

function tail(array $list) {
    foreach ($list as &$entry) { $entry++; }
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 4: Iterate &#39;$amount&#39; by reference and assign to it directly instead of writing through the key.</li>
<li>line 6: &#39;$amount&#39; is not a reference here; unsetting it is unnecessary.</li>
<li>line 8: Unset &#39;$tag&#39; right after the loop: it is still a reference to the last element.</li>
<li>line 13: &#39;$p&#39; is not a reference here; unsetting it is unnecessary.</li>
</ul>

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUGGEST_USING_VALUE_BY_REF | bool | false | Enables part C (D7–D8). Parts A and B are always active. |

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "AlterInForeach": {
      "enabled": false,
      "options": {
        "SUGGEST_USING_VALUE_BY_REF": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore AlterInForeach

/**
 * @noinspection AlterInForeachInspection
 */
```
